Marissa — quick assessment below (replying inline):

> They asked for a 6–12 month reserved capacity proposal; their usage profile is primarily low-latency conversational agents with occasional long-document summarization jobs.

1) SKU raw capabilities (short):
- H100: 80GB HBMe (room for long KV caches), best single-stream decode perf for long-context generation, highest tokens/sec for RT use-cases. Ideal for latency-sensitive decode with high context.
- A100: 40GB HBM, good throughput for batch/medium-length contexts, lower single-stream perf vs H100 for large models; cheaper per-card than H100.
- L4: 24GB, optimized for inference density and embeddings/short-context responses; best cost per-token for small-to-medium models and high concurrency.

2) Memory vs perf tradeoffs (example thresholds):
- If Crestline needs >32k token KV cache or frequent 40k+ context runs, H100 is the only comfortable fit without aggressive offloading.
- Mixed workloads (conversational + background summarization) are served well by H100 primary + L4 for embeddings / bursty parallelizable jobs.

3) Commitment recommendation (ops-safe hedge):
- Phase A (0–3mo): Reserve 4 H100 + 12 L4 (L4 handles embeddings and most short-turn conversational traffic; H100s cover peak low-latency inference).
- Phase B (3–6mo): If p95 latency and utilization justify, expand to 6 H100 (or 4 H100 + 6 A100 depending on pricing/availability) to reduce tail latency.
- Fallback policy: allow up to 30% of committed H100-equivalents to be served by A100s at a defined fallback price with explicit latency SLO adjustments in the SOW.

4) Ops tolerances to document for SOW:
- Allowed fallbacks: 0–15% immediate (no penalty), 15–30% with credit schedule, >30% triggers remediation plan.
- Warm-up lead time for new reserved capacity: 7–14 days depending on region.

I can draft a 1-page technical appendix for the SOW that shows token/sec estimates and memory headroom. Flag anything you want highlighted for procurement.

—Karthik

Thanks Karthik — leaning into a hedged approach makes sense commercially. A few commercial/ops notes: 

- Pricing: H100 list is ~1.9x A100 in our pricing curve; L4 is ~0.25x A100 for tokens/embedding workloads. Any fallback clauses should include clear per-card fallback pricing to avoid disputes.
- Commit phasing PDF attached: shows a 3-phase billing and credit schedule we use (commit_phasing_plan.pdf).
- HubSpot: I put the proposed commit phasing and fallback terms on HS deal 97213 — review there and confirm which pricing tier (Enterprise vs Enterprise Plus) we should quote.

Operational risk callouts: 
- Regional availability of H100 in us-west might be tight in Q1; if Crestline requires regional lock, we need pushback on lead time and consider A100 as a regional hedge.
- SLA language: we should offer a latency SLO for primary H100 paths and a Tiered fallback SLO for when A100/L4 are used. That SLO needs to map to credits we can tolerate.

Next: I can draft fallback pricing lines and a simple SLO table. Marissa — want to run this with legal & procurement once you have approval from Crestline.

Peter / Contracts team — great speaking with you today. Per our discussion, here is the recommended approach we plan to surface in the SOW and commercial terms. Please confirm the high-level ask so we can finalize pricing and a draft SOW: 

Summary of recommended path:
- Phase A (0–3 months): Reserve 4 H100 + 12 L4. L4 instances handle embeddings and background jobs; H100s provide the low-latency production paths.
- Phase B (3–6 months): Expand to 6 H100 if utilization >70% and p95 latency targets are met. Alternative: 4 H100 + 6 A100 if regional H100 capacity is constrained.
- Fallback: Up to 30% of H100-equivalent traffic may be served on A100s (with defined latency SLO adjustments and a fallback price schedule). 0–15% fallback triggers no commercial credit; 15–30% triggers a small credit; >30% triggers a remediation plan.

Requested confirmation items from Crestline: 
1) Confirm that your primary workload is latency-sensitive conversational agents (yes/no).
2) Estimate steady-state QPS and peak tokens/sec per minute for month 1 vs month 6 (spreadsheet attached).
3) Any regulatory/regional constraints (need for on-prem or specific zone reservations).

Attached: crestline_sku_tolerance_v1.xlsx
HubSpot record: HS-97213

If you confirm the profile we can circulate a short SOW appendix + pricing and a 3-month review milestone clause.

Thanks —

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary and for walking through the options. Confirming: our primary workload is latency-sensitive chatbots used customer-facing, with batch long-doc summarization (nightly jobs) as secondary.

We are comfortable starting with Phase A (4 H100 + 12 L4) for a 6-month reserved term, with a formal review at 3 months. A few items we need in the SOW before we sign: 
- Explicit fallback SLO language (what p95/p99 we guarantee on primary vs fallback and credit schedule).
- On-call contact for incidents impacting reserved capacity and an escalation path.
- Confirmation of regional placement: prefer us-west, but can tolerate cross-region failover with 48-hour notice.

Procurement: please send the SOW + pricing and a PO template to contracts@crestline.ai. We will aim to return a signed SOW within two weeks if the SLOs are acceptable.
